 "text": "# TSMC Slumps Nearly 6% as Jensen Huang’s Exit and AI Debt Fears Rattle Investors Ahead of Nvidia Earnings

Six days after reporting record monthly sales, **Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.** [(NYSE:TSM)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TSM) lost about \$106 billion in market value in Taipei on Monday.

**Nvidia Corp.** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA) holds its first earnings call since **Jensen Huang** resigned on Tuesday. Investors will be listening for whether Nvidia will keep helping customers finance their chip purchases.

If buyers take longer to raise money, chip orders could slip. Nvidia is TSMC’s biggest customer and accounts for an estimated 22% of its 2026 sales, according to JPMorgan Asia Pacific Equity [Research](https://am.jpmorgan.com/content/dam/jpm-am-aem/global/en/insights/eye-on-the-market/ai-tracker-amv.pdf).

TSMC shares opened slightly lower in Taiwan on Monday and ended the day down nearly 6%. Foxconn and MediaTek fell even more. Local dealers said Friday’s U.S. tech selloff spilled into Taiwan as investors weighed Nvidia’s future.

### Kress Had Already Pushed Back on Huang’s Deals

At a meeting in Berlin last month, Huang told cloud executives that if they wanted Nvidia chips, they’d need to get customers to pay in advance for the computing power they planned to rent out, The Wall Street Journal [reported](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/nvidias-days-as-an-open-checkbook-for-the-ai-economy-are-numbered-90c7b388).

As Nvidia’s finance chief, **Colette Kress** had already questioned how much the company stood to earn from guaranteeing customers’ data center deals. Over the summer, she reworked a deal to back an OpenAI data center in Ohio, cutting Nvidia’s proposed commitment roughly in half, the Journal [reported](https://www.wsj.com/tech/jensen-huang-colette-kress-nvidia-ceo-eb289097).

Apollo and Blackstone are still discussing deals under Nvidia’s August plan to raise more than \$500 billion from outside investors, according to Reuters. Huang said Nvidia could back up to \$125 billion under that plan.

On Tuesday, Kress will have her first chance as interim CEO to tell investors whether Nvidia is willing to put its own money behind it’s customers orders.

### Huang May Not Be Gone for Good

Huang has discussed a comeback with confidants, the Financial Times [reported](https://www.ft.com/content/45383d86-33c4-4d99-86e5-5e058d3567c1). If he returned as CEO, the man who built the financing plan would be setting its terms again.

[Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/jensen-huang-rejoins-nvidia-byptptpt/will-jensen-huang-rejoin-nvidia-by-december-31-2026) gave him about a 14% chance Monday of an announced return in any formal role by year-end, with \$1.15 million traded on that contract. A board seat would count, so the odds of him running Nvidia again are lower.

Analysts [expect Nvidia’s third-quarter](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/11/63282757/nvidia-must-now-prove-its-bigger-than-jensen-huang) revenue to reach about \$109 billion, but that quarter closed with Huang still in charge. What TSMC investors need is the outlook, and a sense of which buyers Nvidia will still back.

In October, TSMC CEO **C.C. Wei** said the company sends its own teams to U.S. data centers to check on construction and power. Their verdict was \"so far so good.\"

That was before Huang resigned. At 5 p.m. ET Tuesday, interim CEO Colette Kress gives investors their first read since.
